54c937.title: Admin guard audit — results + consulta.ts BOLA candidate
54c937.content:
## Admin guard audit — static results (agent fc8c25e9)

### Verdict on the assigned scope: admin role-check coverage is SOLID
1. **pharmacy.routes.ts** (mounted `/api/admin/pharmacies`, app.ts:363) — has its OWN inline `requireAdmin` (lines 13-20): DB role lookup, fail-closed try/catch→403, applied via `router.use(requireAuth, requireAdmin)` before all 4 routes. No pre-guard routes, no re-mounts. VERIFIED SAFE.
2. **admin.routes.ts** — `router.use(requireAuth)` line 25, `router.use(requireAdmin)` line 33 (DB role check; exception propagates to errorHandler, no fail-open). All 62 routes declared after the guards; none opt out; no nested mounts. All privileged actions named in the task (settings `saveSettings`, push global/campaign, credits adjust `PATCH /users/:id/credits`, plan, block/unblock, reset-mfa, tickets manage, ai-config, labs CRUD, api-access approve/reject, api-keys revoke, PII lookup/reveal) live here behind the guard.
3. **Role escalation — RULED OUT**: schema.prisma:19 `role Role @default(OWNER)`. Only 2 `user.create` sites (auth.routes.ts:208,270) omit role → default. No `user.update` writes role/plan/blocked/tokenVersion outside admin routes. PATCH /me allowlists 3 fields (no spread). data.routes /import creates only user-scoped child objects.
4. **Settings — RULED OUT**: `saveSettings` only from admin.routes.ts:232,255. `/api/patients/demo-event` (patient.routes.ts:31) writes ONLY its own `demoMetrics` key, values are Number(cur)+0/1 — no key/value injection.
5. **Audit middleware**: accessAudit AREAS regex covers `/api/admin`; allowlist skips some areas but is monitoring-only (not an authz control). auditLog.ts console-only fallback for doctor actors = logging gap, not bypass. Sensitive admin actions (PII lookup/reveal) have inline `audit()` calls.

### Mount classification (app.ts:256-404) — all 33 routers
- **Public**: `/api/public/decifre`, `/api/public/lead`, `/api/public/v1` (API-key), `/api/docs`, `/api/webhooks/*`, `/api/labs` (GET list + logo only), `/api/doctor/crm`, direct `app.get`: health, build-info, app/version, privacidade/termos, robots, sitemap, api-docs redirect, `public/config`, `notifications/unsubscribe` (signed token), `public/shared/:token` (PIN+shareLimiter), `patients/:id/photo` (requirePhotoToken).
- **requireAuth only** (object-level scoping per handler — BOLA surface, separate audit): patients, mental-screening, exams, items, analyses, chat, reminders, billing, measurements, medications (GET /pharmacies public by design), risk, vaccines, expenses, devices, notifications, consulta, data, achievements, tickets, sports, doctor-shares, doctor-questions.
- **requireAuth+requireAdmin**: `/api/admin`, `/api/admin/pharmacies`.
- **requireDoctor** (JWT `type:'doctor'`): `/api/doctor` — public exceptions: register/google/verify-email/login/mfa/verify + GET /crm (rate-limited); requireAuth: lookup, specialties; requirePhotoToken: photo/:id; `GET /patients/:patientId/exams/:examId/file` (line 571) has NO requireDoctor arg but does INLINE `verifyDoctorToken` + active doctorShare + `scopes.includes('exams')` + examIds check — verified equivalent protection (doctor.routes.ts:571-589).

### CANDIDATE for BOLA validation agents (outside admin scope, flagged):
- **consulta.ts POST /api/consulta/exams/:examId** (lines 7-19): `requireAuth` only; `prisma.exam.findUnique({ where: { id: req.params.examId } })` with **NO ownerId/userPatientIds scoping** (sibling routes all scope). Response embeds patient full name, age (dateOfBirth), clinical profile, requesting doctor, source lab, and ALL abnormal exam item values (LGPD sensitive). Any authenticated OWNER with another user's examId (cuid) reads another patient's health data. Coverage entry `61cda1` (needs_follow_up) — needs dynamic PoC.

171e93.title: bola-candidates
171e93.content:
White-box BOLA/IDOR discovery sweep — /workspace/server/src/routes/*.ts (all 32 route files) + app.ts photo route. Mount points from app.ts; tenant model: Patient.ownerId → req.userId, `requireAuth` authenticates only.

## P1 — CONFIRMED BY CODE READ (validation agent should PoC)

**1. POST /api/consulta/exams/:examId — exam fetched by bare ID, zero ownership check**
- File: `src/routes/consulta.ts:10-27` (mount app.ts:395 → `/api/consulta`)
- Handler: `prisma.exam.findUnique({ where: { id: String(req.params.examId) } })` then builds a full "Preparo de Consulta" HTML page: patient full name, age, clinical profile (`patient.clinicalProfile`), exam title/lab/requesting doctor, up to 10 ABNORMAL lab values with flags, plus prior-exam comparison (also unscoped).
- Missing check: no `userPatientIds(req.userId)` / `ownerId` verification anywhere in file (contrast: exam.routes.ts uses `loadOwnedExam` for the same object).
- Impact: any authenticated user with any other user's exam CUID reads another person's health data (LGPD sensitive). Requires knowing/guessing exam CUID (non-enumerable, but leaked in shares/links/tickets).
- Confidence: high (static trace; trivial PoC with 2 users + supertest).

**2. GET /api/items?patientId=<other-users-patientId> — scope overwritten by raw query param**
- File: `src/routes/item.routes.ts:347-348` (mount app.ts:330 → `/api/items`)
- `const where = { exam: { patientId: { in: pids } } }; if (q.patientId) where.exam = { patientId: q.patientId };` — the pids filter is REPLACED by the attacker-supplied patientId with NO `pids.includes` check. Every sibling handler in the same file (timeseries:95-99, distinct-names:164-168, evolution:207-211, flag-summary:295-299, abnormal:328-332) validates `pids.includes(...)` — only the LIST route forgot it.
- Impact: full paginated listing of another tenant's ExamItem rows (lab analyte values, flags, refs) — health data at scale.
- Confidence: high.

## P2 — SECONDARY OBSERVATIONS (lower priority / other agents' scope)

**3. GET /api/patients/:id/photo (app.ts:297-299, `requirePhotoToken`)** — any VALID JWT (any patient user OR doctor, any tenant) + patient CUID → serves patient facial photo. `requirePhotoToken` (middleware/auth.ts:19-26) only verifies signature, no subject/tenant binding. Same class as threat-model item 5. CUID secrecy is the only barrier — LGPD facial data. Flagged for validation (cross-tenant photo read).
**4. POST /api/medications/refresh-all (medication.routes.ts:701)** — auth-only global wipe of ALL MedicationPriceSnapshot rows + requeue of every user's medications (availability/integrity side effect). BFLA-ish, not BOLA — hand to admin-routes agent if any.
**5. doctor-share POST/PATCH accepts `examIds` array unvalidated** (doctor-share.routes.ts:53,91) — examIds not verified against owner's exams. Doctor-side queries still scope by patientId, so worst case is a share row referencing foreign exam CUIDs that never match queries → information-set is patient-scoped. Low; note only.
**6. GET /api/billing/payment-status/:id MP fallback (billing.routes.ts:950)** — if no local Subscription matches, proxies payment status from Mercado Pago API for any payment id; leaks only MP status string, no PII. Informational.

## RULED OUT (named controls, per file)
- patient.routes.ts — `pids.includes(id)` on GET/:id (:282-284), PUT (:323-327), DELETE (:342-346), POST photo (:328-332 area), health-score/summary/dashboard (123-125, 152-154, 166-168); list `ownerId` (:103).
- exam.routes.ts — `loadOwnedExam` guard (findUnique + pids check) on GET/:id, /file, DELETE, /reextract; attest replicates guard; list scoped `patientId in pids`; upload validates patientId ∈ pids.
- item.routes.ts — all handlers except LIST (above) validate `pids.includes`.
- analysis.routes.ts — `loadOwnedAnalysis` (resolves patientId via exam) on GET/:id, /chat, /share, DELETE /share; LIST guards examId via userExamIds sentinel.
- medication.routes.ts — PATCH/DELETE/:id, GET /:id/prices, /:id/event-signals, /:id/process-price all re-check `pids.includes(m.patientId)` post-fetch; lists create with pid ∈ pids.
- measurement.routes.ts — DELETE checks pids; GET/POST/activity-sync derive pid via `pids.includes(...) ?? pids[0]`.
- vaccine/expense/reminder/notification/ticket/device — ownerId or pids checks (`expense.ownerId !== req.userId` :50; reminder :54/:74; notification updateMany userId :31; ticket userId checks :59/:124/:147).
- mental-screening.routes.ts — all 3 handlers `pids.includes(pid)` 403.
- risk.routes.ts — every patientId gate `pids.includes` (assess/latest/adherence/predictions/feedback/consent/action-plan).
- sports.routes.ts — firstPatientId/userPatientIds derived; PUT profile rejects `wanted ∉ pids` (:102).
- achievement/chat/data.routes — userId or pids everywhere (export uses gatherExportData with pids).
- doctor-question.routes.ts — list/detail filter `patientId in pids`; create derives pid ∈ pids + requires active share.
- doctor-share.routes.ts — PATCH/DELETE `pids.includes(share.patientId)`.
- doctor.routes.ts — all /patients/:patientId/* behind `requireDoctor` + active DoctorShare (many also check `scopes.includes('exams')` + examIds subset); exam file route (:571) manually verifies doctor token + share + scopes + examIds; notes/questions/invites/goals/reviews bind doctorId/token-match (requireGoalAccess/requireReviewAccess check `req.params.doctorId === req.doctorId`).
- billing.routes.ts — pending-payment/pending/:id/payment-status scoped `userId: req.userId`; status/credits/history scoped userId/pids.
- admin.routes.ts / pharmacy.routes.ts — `router.use(requireAuth, requireAdmin)` role gate (BFLA agent to verify in depth).
- public-api.routes.ts — meds/prices/interactions operate on client-supplied data or global catalog; keys delete checks `row.userId !== req.userId` (:377-379).
- labs/lead/decifre/openpix/asaas — no per-object tenant reads (labs logo public by design; decifre/lead public tools with no PII persistence; webhooks keyed by provider payload — separate agent).
- auth.routes.ts — no `req.params` object routes (session-scoped via req.userId).

0f1ced.title: static-triage-results
0f1ced.content: Static triage of /workspace/server (Express 5 + Prisma 6 + TS). All artifacts in /workspace/.source-aware/. Web-search unavailable → CVE data from trivy offline GHSA DB. ## P0 — BOLA candidates (validation agents: highest value) 1. **POST /api/consulta/exams/:examId — missing ownership check** (`src/routes/consulta.ts:11`). Handler does `prisma.exam.findUnique({ where: { id } })` with NO `userPatientIds`/ownerId filter, then returns full HTML: patient name, age, clinical profile, requesting doctor, lab, and all abnormal lab values. Every other route file uses `pids.includes(...)`; this one forgot. Any authenticated OWNER who knows/guesses any examId (CUID, non-enumerable but leaked in shares/other responses) reads another user's clinical data. Route mounted at app.ts:395 (`/api/consulta`), requireAuth at consulta.ts:7. Also has unescaped `${name}`/`${exam.title}` interpolation into HTML (XSS candidate — rawExtraction.patientName is attacker-influenced via uploaded PDF) — separate finding, same file. 2. **requirePhotoToken accepts any valid JWT for any patient photo** (`src/middleware/auth.ts:19`). Signature+expiry only; no userId binding, no blocked/tokenVersion check. `/api/patients/:id/photo` (app.ts:296-318) and `/api/doctor/photo/:id` (doctor.routes.ts:455) serve facial PII to any token holder. Known/accepted-risk design per comments, but LGPD facial data + no revocation — needs dynamic validation + severity call. ## P1 — Secrets (gitleaks+trufflehog verified; ALL real, none placeholder) - `.env:22` APP_ENCRYPTION_KEY (64-hex AES-256 CPF/PII key) - `.env:52` ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN (sk-style proxy token) - `.env:68` ML_CLIENT_SECRET + `.env:69` ML_REFRESH_TOKEN (MercadoLivre OAuth) - `.env:72` FIRECRAWL_API_KEY - `.env:46` MP_ACCESS_TOKEN = `APP_USR-...` (Mercado Pago PRODUCTION access token; gitleaks generic rule missed it — match is real) - `.env:40` SMTP_PASS (real-looking) - `.env` also: CONSULTA_CRM_KEY, GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID, DATABASE_URL with credentials - `janocaminho-minhasaude-firebase-adminsdk-fbsvc-a3865e8e4e.json:5` — full Firebase service-account PRIVATE KEY (RSA). Trufflehog corroborates (PrivateKey + GCP detectors); full-repo trufflehog rerun (excl. node_modules) found nothing beyond this. - `.gitignore` does NOT ignore `.env` (only test fixtures) → these would be committed in any git init. No .git dir in sandbox (repo mounted without it). - Deeper `.env` secrets not in .env.example (ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN etc.) → real live values, not samples. NODE_ENV=development. ## P2 — Injection candidates (need dynamic validation) - **XSS via HTML interpolation of patient/exam data** (semgrep raw-html-format, all verified by read): - `src/app.ts:452-462` `/api/public/shared/:token` — `patientName`, `exam.title`, `lab` unescaped into public HTML page (contentMd is escaped; names/titles are NOT). Attacker: patient sets own name to `` at registration (auth.routes.ts:211/273, String(name) unsanitized) → stored XSS fires in doctor's browser when opening shared report. LGPD context amplifies. - `src/routes/consulta.ts:52-96` — `name` (from rawExtraction.patientName — attacker controls via uploaded PDF!), `lab`, `doctor`, `profile`, `exam.title`, item names/values unescaped into returned HTML. - `src/app.ts:389-390` unsubscribe page — `first` (user.name first word) unescaped; link/token encoded properly. - `detect-non-literal-regexp` (15 hits): ReDoS candidates in pricing providers (vtexDynamic.ts:40,44, vtexMulti.ts:36,38, pacheco.ts:34,36, pagueMenos.ts:46,48, mercadoLivre.ts:31), analysis (clinical-trials.ts:105, guidelines.ts:85, sports-knowledge.ts:79), utils (interactions.ts:64, normalize.ts:108), public-api.routes.ts:177. Values come from scraping/DB — moderate. - **Raw SQL is SAFE**: all `$queryRawUnsafe` calls (subscriptionCompat.ts:101,137,183) use parameterized values + allowlisted column names; admin.routes.ts raw queries are fully static. No injection found. - orderBy all static. No SQLi surface beyond above. - `unsafe-formatstring` INFO hits (10) all reviewed: benign console.error/warn logging, no format-string sink. ## P3 — Config/defense-in-depth - All rate limiters `skip: NODE_ENV !== 'production'` (app.ts:95-105, decifre.routes.ts:29) — decifre (public AI endpoint), signup, share-PIN brute-force protections OFF in dev. - CORS check + skipDev pattern needs runtime confirmation. - JWT_SECRET present in .env (non-default); prod boot guard exists (config.ts:144-149). - tokenVersion revocation tolerant to legacy tokens without `ver` claim (auth.ts:58-63) — accepted-risk comment, dynamic check worthwhile. - gitleaks note: `src/jobs/auditRetention.ts` hit an OOM during the gitleaks run only; trufflehog full rerun scanned it clean. ## P4 — Dependency CVEs (filed via create_dependency_report) - vuln-0001 sharp 0.32.6 HIGH — reachable (optimizeAvatar on all uploads, `failOn:'none'`) → memory corruption on untrusted images. - vuln-0002 nodemailer 9.1.1 HIGH — reachable (sendEmail to attacker-controlled addresses; lead regex allows quoted local-parts). - vuln-0003 node-forge 1.4.0 LOW (imported only via firebase-admin; no app path). - vuln-0004 deepmerge-ts 7.1.5 LOW (not imported; @prisma/config internal). - vuln-0005 uuid 10.0.0 INFO (not imported). - Express 5.2.1, @prisma/client 6.19.3, multer 2.4.0, imapflow 2.2.11, mailparser 3.9.37, qrcode 1.5.4, jsonwebtoken 9.0.3, @sentry/node 10.76.1, zod 4.6.5: no known CVEs in trivy DB at scan time. - Archiver/pdf-parse/firebase-admin/bcryptjs/express-rate-limit/@anthropic-ai/sdk present in package.json but NOT installed in node_modules (partial install) — versions unresolvable, not scannable. ## Coverage conclusions (static-only, needs dynamic) - Admin routes: BOTH `/api/admin` (admin.routes.ts:25,33) and `/api/admin/pharmacies` (pharmacy.routes.ts:20) run requireAuth+requireAdmin before any route → admin-without-role-check story RULED OUT statically. - Webhooks: OpenPix + Asaas both fail-closed with server-side provider verification (openpix-webhook.routes.ts:82-97, asaas-webhook.routes.ts:99+) → billing spoofing story largely defended statically; residual risk = provider API outage handling (fetch error → treated as not-confirmed, still fail-closed). - BOLA sweep of ~30 route files: ALL have pids/ownerId checks EXCEPT consulta.ts (P0 above). exam/item/analysis/measurement/medication/reminder/vaccine/expense/mental-screening/risk/sports/chat/data/device/ticket/doctor-share all scope correctly. Doctor routes verify DoctorShare scopes+examIds. - Public PII: lead (honeypot+hash), decifre (nothing persisted), public-api (requireApiKey), shared reports (CUID token + 6-digit PIN + limiter). Main gap = unescaped interpolation above. ## Artifacts (all bounded, /workspace/.source-aware/, 536K total) semgrep.json (54 findings), sg-targets.txt (178 files), ast-grep.json (compacted per-file census of 11526 matches), gitleaks.json (6), trufflehog.json + trufflehog2.log (full-repo rerun), trivy-fs.json + trivy-synth.json (synthetic lockfile from 498 installed pkgs), synth-lock/.

eb6576.title: webhook-spoof-analysis
eb6576.content:
# Billing webhook spoofing — verdict: BLOCKED (ruled out, dynamic PoC + full static trace)

## TL;DR
The attacker story in the threat model (register → buy-credits → read paymentId → POST public webhook with forged COMPLETED payload → free premium/credits) is **real up to the provider check, then stops**. Both webhooks (`/api/webhooks/openpix`, `/api/webhooks/asaas`) are public and NOT HMAC-signed, and the match key (`mpPaymentId`) is client-visible — but every approval path ends in a **server-side provider verification** (GET charge/payment at the provider, fail-closed), added in an audit "10/26". A forged webhook cannot approve anything: **7/7 dynamic PoC tests pass proving block; control test proves the chain would grant +140 credits if the provider confirmed**.

## The chain, step by step (all steps statically verified, dynamically proven where runnable)
1. **paymentId is client-visible** — `src/routes/billing.routes.ts`: buy-credits PIX returns `paymentId: charge.id` (line 435; plan variant line 300; api-pack line 853; pay-card line 601/605). For OpenPix, `charge.id` IS the correlationID (`src/payments/pix-provider.ts:209` — `id: String(charge.correlationID ?? input.correlationID)`), stored as `mpPaymentId`. correlationID formats: `credits_<subId>_<n>`, `plan_<subId>`, `api_<subId>_<n>` (billing.routes.ts:287, 355, 813). Also re-exposed by GET `/api/billing/pending-payment` (`paymentId: pending.mpPaymentId`, line 907) and 409 pendingPix payloads (lines 229-231, 322-324, 520-522).
2. **Webhooks are public & unsigned** — mounted in app.ts without requireAuth; OpenPix has no native HMAC; Asaas payload unsigned. No IP allowlist, no secret header, no HMAC anywhere in these two handlers (verified by full read + grep for allowlist/signature).
3. **Payload status leniency confirmed**: OpenPix handler skips the status check when `status` is empty (`openpix-webhook.routes.ts:32` — `if (status && status !== 'COMPLETED')`); Asaas accepts `event.startsWith('PAYMENT_RECEIVED')` OR status ∈ {RECEIVED, RECEIVED_IN_CASH, CONFIRMED, DETERMINED} (`asaas-webhook.routes.ts:26-29`). Amount must **exactly equal** `round(sub.amount*100)` cents — but sub.amount is server-side (from pack settings), and the client LEARNS it from the buy response (`price`), so amount equality is NOT a barrier to a knowing attacker.
4. **THE CONTROL — provider verification** (this is what kills the attack):
   - OpenPix: `openpix-webhook.routes.ts:81-95` — after sub lookup + PENDING + amount, requires `hasOpenPix()` (else 400 fail-closed) and `fetch(openPixApiBaseUrl/api/v1/charge/<correlationID>)` with the App ID; requires `charge.status === 'COMPLETED'` from the provider else 400. Forged correlationID → provider returns not-found → blocked. A REAL unpaid charge returns PENDING → blocked.
   - Asaas: `asaas-webhook.routes.ts:93-109` — same pattern: `hasAsaas()` gate, `GET /v3/payments/<id>` with `access_token`, status must be in RECEIVED set else 400. Provider down / non-ok / exception → treated as NOT confirmed (fail closed, comment line 104).
   - MP webhook (`billing.routes.ts:958-1016`): ENFORCES x-signature HMAC when `MP_WEBHOOK_SECRET` set (401 on bad sig, lines 966-982); when unset logs DEV warning, but still fetches the payment from MP's API (line 988) and only approves on `pay.status === 'approved'` (line 998) — a forged `data.id` returns 404/non-approved from MP → no approval. **Caveat (minor, config-dependent)**: without MP_WEBHOOK_SECRET there is no replay-protection, but approval still requires a real approved payment at MP, so spoofing cannot mint value.
5. **pay-card inline** (`billing.routes.ts:466-607`): approves locally ONLY when provider charge.status ∈ {CONFIRMED, RECEIVED, DETERMINED} (line 592) — the status comes from `createAsaasCardCharge`'s response, not client input. Not spoofable by request.
6. **jobs/pix-expiry.ts race**: expiry job cancels PENDING subs; approval requires `status === 'PENDING'` checked inside the webhook, and `approvePendingSubscription` re-checks `status !== 'APPROVED'` for idempotency. No double-credit: approval sets APPROVED transactionally; expiry only flips PENDING→CANCELLED. A race between approve and cancel at worst loses an approval (paid user not credited — availability nit, not spoofing). No window where a cancelled sub gets credited (kind re-check uses sub fields; credits>0 enforced).
7. **Amount mismatch** (`openpix:72-78`, `asaas:82-88`): exact cents equality — not attacker-relevant (they know the price) but blocks amount-tampering.

## Dynamic PoC (RAN, 7/7 PASS — `test/poc-webhook-spoof.test.ts`, `npx vitest run test/poc-webhook-spoof.test.ts`)
- OpenPix forged COMPLETED (id+exact amount) on own PENDING sub → **400 "Cobrança não confirmada no provider."**, credits stay 0, sub stays PENDING. ✅
- OpenPix forged with EMPTY status (skips payload status filter) → **400**, no credit. ✅
- Asaas forged PAYMENT_RECEIVED on `pay_*` PENDING → **400**, no credit. ✅
- PLAN spoof (`plan_<subId>`) → **400**, `planExpiresAt` stays null. ✅
- CONTROL: provider mock says COMPLETED → same webhook approves, +140 credits → proves the chain grants value and only the provider check stops it. ✅
- INFO: `/billing/pending-payment` returns `paymentId` to owner (chain enabler confirmed). ✅
- Missing config → fail CLOSED (400), never blind-approves. ✅

## Residual risks (for the reporting agent — NOT spoofable-grant, but hardening notes)
1. **No IP allowlist / no signature** on the two public webhooks: any internet host can spam them. Each hit causes a provider GET (potential provider-side rate-limit/quota exhaustion → self-DoS via third-party API). Cheap to fix with OpenPix's IP list / Asaas `asaas-access-token` header check.
2. **MP webhook without `MP_WEBHOOK_SECRET`** accepts unsigned payloads — still provider-verified, but a defense-in-depth gap (replay/spam, log noise, rawWebhook overwrite: line ~992 `updateMany({where:{id: subIdRef}, data:{rawWebhook: pay}})` lets a forged-but-provider-valid id overwrite audit data of a sub with a known id — sub ids are cuids, low risk).
3. The provider verification relies on **charge-by-correlationID**: for OpenPix, an attacker who *actually pays* their own charge gets approved — that's by design (it's a payment), not spoofing.
4. **Fail-open environment risk is absent**: both webhooks fail closed without credentials (verified in test).

## Verdict
- **Webhook spoofing → ruled_out** (named controls: `openpix-webhook.routes.ts:81-95` and `asaas-webhook.routes.ts:93-109` provider GET + fail-closed checks, on every approval path; MP: HMAC at `billing.routes.ts:966-982` + provider status check line 988/998).
- Residual: unauthorized-spam/DoS-of-provider surface (medium/low hardening), MP unsigned-in-dev note.

Harness notes for other agents: vitest works — run with LONG timeout (~200s: transform+import are slow, `import 178s`); first run needed `node_modules` install + Linux prisma engine symlink `node_modules/.prisma/client/libquery_engine-debian-openssl-3.0.x.so.node -> ../../@prisma/engines/libquery_engine-debian-openssl-3.0.x.so.node` (client was generated on Windows). DB `127.0.0.1:5433/meus_exames_test` is up.

4e09b7.content:
# Test Harness — PostgreSQL + vitest (dynamic validation infrastructure)

## Status: WORKING (2026-10-08)
PostgreSQL 18.6 running as `pentester` (no service/systemd):
- Data dir: `/workspace/.pgdata`
- Listen: `127.0.0.1:5433` (TCP) — unix socket in `/workspace/.pgdata` (NOT `/var/run/postgresql` — permission denied there)
- Log: `/workspace/.pgdata/postgres.log`
- Role: `meus_exames` / `meus_exames_dev` (SUPERUSER, trust auth on TCP? no — password via pg_hba default; role has LOGIN)
- DB: `meus_exames_test`, 58 tables, schema applied via `prisma db push --accept-data-loss`

## DATABASE_URL (export before anything)
```bash
export DATABASE_URL='postgresql://meus_exames:meus_exames_dev@127.0.0.1:5433/meus_exames_test?schema=public'
```
Note: `test/setup.ts` sets this itself (unless TEST_DATABASE_URL overrides) — the vitest suite does NOT need the env var, but `prisma` CLI commands DO.

## Restart if postgres dies
```bash
/usr/lib/postgresql/18/bin/pg_ctl -D /workspace/.pgdata -l /workspace/.pgdata/postgres.log -w start
# verify: /usr/lib/postgresql/18/bin/pg_isready -h 127.0.0.1 -p 5433
# stop:   ... pg_ctl -D /workspace/.pgdata stop   (DO NOT — leave running)
```

## Reset DB from scratch (only if schema drifts)
```bash
/usr/lib/postgresql/18/bin/pg_ctl -D /workspace/.pgdata -w stop || true
rm -rf /workspace/.pgdata && sudo mkdir -p /workspace/.pgdata && sudo chown pentester:pentester /workspace/.pgdata && chmod 700 /workspace/.pgdata
/usr/lib/postgresql/18/bin/initdb -D /workspace/.pgdata -U postgres --auth=trust -E UTF8
printf "listen_addresses = '127.0.0.1'\nport = 5433\nunix_socket_directories = '/workspace/.pgdata'\n" >> /workspace/.pgdata/postgresql.conf
/usr/lib/postgresql/18/bin/pg_ctl -D /workspace/.pgdata -l /workspace/.pgdata/postgres.log -w start
/usr/lib/postgresql/18/bin/psql -h 127.0.0.1 -p 5433 -U postgres -c "CREATE ROLE meus_exames LOGIN PASSWORD 'meus_exames_dev' SUPERUSER;" -c "CREATE DATABASE meus_exames_test OWNER meus_exames;"
cd /workspace/server && export DATABASE_URL='postgresql://meus_exames:meus_exames_dev@127.0.0.1:5433/meus_exames_test?schema=public'
npx prisma db push --skip-generate --accept-data-loss && npx prisma generate
```

## Verified GREEN test files (run from /workspace/server)
- `npx vitest run test/auth.test.ts` — 9/9 passed (register/login/CPF/OTP/requireAuth/forgot-reset)
- `npx vitest run test/billing.test.ts test/asaas-webhook.test.ts` — 21/21 passed (12 billing + 9 asaas-webhook: plan activation, idempotent webhooks, credit packs, PIX lifecycle)
- `test/setup.ts` mocks ALL externals (mailer→no-op, storage, Anthropic, MP/Asaas/OpenPix fetch stubs) and forces NODE_ENV=test. Safe to run any test file.

## QUIRKS (important)
1. **Non-TTY exec_command swallows output** — ALWAYS pass `tty:true`.
2. **node_modules was broken on arrival** (~9 pkgs, `effect` MODULE_NOT_FOUND). Fixed by `npm install` after temporarily removing `@meus-exames/shared` from package.json deps (that workspace pkg does not exist in this sandbox). package.json was RESTORED to original afterwards. If npm install is re-run as-is it will fail 404 on `@meus-exames/shared` — either tolerate or temporarily strip that one dep line again.
3. **`@meus-exames/shared` is stubbed** at `node_modules/@meus-exames/shared` (empty module, types for ScreeningType/PHQ9_ITEMS/GAD7_ITEMS/validateScreeningAnswers/scoreScreening/severityOf/hasSuicidalIdeation/maxScoreOf/screeningItems). Real logic only used by `src/routes/mental-screening.routes.ts` + `test/mental-health.test.ts` — those will FAIL or misbehave; everything else unaffected. Any `npm install` / `npm prune` may wipe the stub — re-copy from `/tmp/meus-exames-stub/node_modules/@meus-exames/shared` if missing.
4. **`prisma migrate deploy` FAILS** (`column "credits" of relation "users" does not exist` — migrations out of sync). Use `prisma db push --accept-data-loss` instead. Without `--accept-data-loss` it hangs on an interactive y/N prompt that piping hides.
5. **Sibling agents share the DB and node_modules**: a concurrent `npm install` raced mine mid-run (EPERM on prisma client copy — retried OK). vitest config is `fileParallelism:false` precisely because tests TRUNCATE shared tables — never run two vitest suites concurrently against the same DB, they will interfere.
6. First vitest run per file is SLOW (~5min wall for ~5s of tests — TS transform/import is ~330s). Subsequent runs of the same file are faster (transform cache). Budget accordingly; prefer re-running only the file you care about.
7. psql pager: set `PAGER=cat` / `-P pager=off` in scripts to avoid `[END]` hangs.
8. `.env` DATABASE_URL points to DB `meus_exames` (not `_test`) on the same port/user — tests override via setup.ts; for `tsx`-run scripts (seed.ts) export the `_test` URL explicitly or they'll hit a DB that doesn't exist.

## For dynamic PoC work
- Server bootstrap: tests import the express app directly (supertest, no listen) — copy that pattern from any test file (e.g. `test/billing.test.ts` header).
- JWT: `process.env.JWT_SECRET='test-secret'` (set by setup.ts).
- Direct DB inspection: `/usr/lib/postgresql/18/bin/psql -h 127.0.0.1 -p 5433 -U meus_exames -d meus_exames_test -P pager=off -c '...'`

e44fb5.title: sqli-injection-candidates — SQL sinks all clean; photoUrl storage-ref path traversal CONFIRMED
e44fb5.content:
## SQL / raw-injection audit — /workspace/server

**Sweep**: `rg '\$queryRaw|\$executeRaw|queryRawUnsafe|executeRawUnsafe'` → 40 hits, all inventoried. No SQL injection found anywhere. One **confirmed non-SQL injection** (path traversal → arbitrary file read) surfaced by the sweep.

### 1) Raw SQL sinks — all ruled out (static/parameterized)
- `src/routes/admin.routes.ts:469,472,481,510-552,595,607,1081` — ~30 `$queryRaw` tagged-template queries. Every string is fully static (no `${}` interpolation at all). Admin search (`/users?q=`, `/payments?status=&q=`, `/exams?status=`, `/audit` filters) flows through the Prisma query builder (parameterized). Behind `requireAuth`+`requireAdmin`.
- `src/utils/subscriptionCompat.ts:101,137,183` — `$queryRawUnsafe`/`$executeRawUnsafe`, but column names come from the hardcoded `BASE_COLUMNS` const (line 26/36) or the allowlist∩schema-columns filter at lines 157-166; values are always `$n` placeholders. Route-reachable (billing/webhooks) but not injectable.
- `src/utils/list.ts:29-33` + `src/routes/exam.routes.ts:52-56` — `_sort`/`_order` from query string; `exam.routes.ts:54` allowlists sort to `['title','performedAt','createdAt','kind','status']` else falls back to `{performedAt:'desc'}`. Prisma `orderBy` (not SQL). All other list routes ignore sort. Dynamic negative control executed: `GET /api/exams?_sort=title;SELECT 1--&q=' OR '1'='1` → 200, empty rows, no error.
- `src/app.ts:117`, `src/jobs/pix-expiry.ts:18-20` — static literals.
- `scripts/qa-reset-test-schema.ts:9-10` — DROP/CREATE SCHEMA literals, not route-reachable → n/a.

### 2) CONFIRMED — storage-ref path traversal → arbitrary local file read (disk mode)
- **Source**: `PUT /api/patients/:id` — `src/routes/patient.routes.ts:380` `if (photoUrl !== undefined) data.photoUrl = photoUrl ? String(photoUrl) : null;` (zero validation; body field, any authenticated OWNER on own patient).
- **Sink**: `GET /api/patients/:id/photo?t=<any valid JWT>` — `src/app.ts:309-313`: `if (p?.photoUrl && !p.photoUrl.startsWith('/api/')) { const r = await resolvePatientPhoto(p.photoUrl); ... res.sendFile(path.resolve(r.file)) }`. Disk mode: `resolvePatientPhoto` (`src/utils/storage.ts:131-141`) returns the ref verbatim → `sendFile` serves ANY existing path. The only guard (`!startsWith('/api/')`) is bypassed by absolute paths and `../` traversal.
- **PoC** (`/workspace/server/poc-sqli-standalone.ts`, real storage, disk mode — `.env` has no S3_BUCKET so this is the deployment's actual mode):
  - `photoUrl="/tmp/poc-secret-marker.txt"` → GET serves marker `POC-PHOTO-TRAVERSAL-...` ✓
  - `photoUrl="../../../../../../../../etc/hostname"` → GET serves exact `/etc/hostname` contents (`f492e185c4e1`) ✓
  - Auth needed: any self-registered user's own patient; read requires any valid JWT (`requirePhotoToken` accepts any token for any patient id).
- **S3-mode variant (untested)**: with `S3_BUCKET` set, same flow presigns `GetObjectCommand({Key: attacker_ref})` → arbitrary-key read across the whole bucket (incl. other patients' exam PDFs under `meus-exames/`).
- **Shared sink, safe sources**: `GET /api/labs/:id/logo` (public!) and `GET /api/doctor/photo/:id` call the same `resolvePatientPhoto`, but their refs (`lab.logoUrl`, `doctor.photoUrl`) are only set via admin/doctor uploads → not attacker-controlled today; fix should still validate refs at the sink.
- **Fix direction**: validate stored refs at update time (must match storage-generated shape) AND contain at serve time (disk mode: `path.resolve(ref)` must stay under `config.photosDir`; S3: key must start with `config.s3Prefix`).

### 3) Non-SQL sweep (while in scope)
- Command injection: extraction pipeline (`pdftotext`/`pdftoppm`/`tesseract`/`convert`) and `mercadoLivre` curl — all `execFile` argv arrays on server-generated temp paths, no shell → ruled out.
- `data.routes.ts` export/import — Prisma-only, streams only own exam files → no injection.

### Harness notes
- vitest currently impractical (box load avg ~7-9 from sibling agents; app import alone takes 60-160s). PoC run standalone via `npx tsx poc-sqli-standalone.ts`.
- Created isolated DB `meus_exames_test_sqli` (schema pushed) to dodge sibling DB contention; can be dropped after.
- `test/poc-sqli.test.ts` written (unmocks storage) for when the box is quiet; it uses `vi.unmock` + the shared test DB.

1fcfaf.title: pii-leak-candidates (findings, prioritized)
1fcfaf.content: PII Leak Audit — public/unauthenticated endpoints of packages/server. Method: full route-inventory scan (app.ts mount order + per-file guards) + source trace + dynamic supertest validation (in-process, test DB 127.0.0.1:5433, app bundled via esbuild to dodge slow module resolution; vitest hangs in this sandbox). ## Unauthenticated endpoint inventory (mounted before/without requireAuth) - `/api/auth/*`: login, register, verify-email, forgot, reset, otp/request, otp/verify, google, mfa/verify (+ doctor variants under `/api/doctor`) - `/api/public/decifre` (rate 3/day/IP), `/api/public/lead`, `/api/public/config`, `/api/public/v1/*` (API-key gated except `GET /`), `/api/public/shared/:token` (PIN gate + shareLimiter 10/15min) - `/api/patients/:id/photo` + `/api/doctor/photo/:id` (requirePhotoToken — ANY valid JWT, no ownership) - `/api/labs`, `/api/labs/:id/logo`; `/api/doctor/crm` (CFM public registry, signupLimiter 8/h); `/api/doctor/invites/by-token/:token` - `/api/health`, `/api/build-info`, `/api/app/version`, `/api/notifications/unsubscribe`, `/api/docs` (swagger), webhooks `/api/webhooks/{openpix,asaas}`, `/api/billing/plans` + `/api/billing/webhook` - Static SPA in prod; `/robots.txt`, `/sitemap.xml`, `/privacidade` (static, no PII) - `POST /api/items/explain` — declared before `router.use(requireAuth)`, but has its own dual (patient-or-doctor) token check; returns only global educational dictionary content by analyte name. Clean. - `GET /api/doctor/patients/:pid/exams/:eid/file` — no requireDoctor in chain but verifies doctor JWT inline + active share + scope + examIds allowlist. Clean. ## FINDINGS (prioritized) ### P1 — CRITICAL (dynamically confirmed): BOLA in POST /api/consulta/exams/:examId leaks full clinical PII of ANY patient to ANY authenticated user - `src/routes/consulta.ts:7` (`router.use(requireAuth)`) + `src/routes/consulta.ts:10-22`: `prisma.exam.findUnique({ where: { id } })` with NO `userPatientIds`/ownership filter — unlike every sibling route. - Leaks (PoC, attacker = unrelated registered user): patient full name, AGE (from dateOfBirth), clinicalProfile (incl. mental-health meds in PoC: "sertralina"), exam title, lab, all abnormal values with ranges, prior-exam evolution, requesting doctor. Response is a ready-to-print HTML document. - Verified: 200 + name/profile/values/age all present; no-token → 401 (auth-only, not anonymous). LGPD Art.5 II sensitive health data at single-request scale. This also hands an attacker victim Patient CUIDs? (No — examId is the input; examIds are CUIDs, also hard to guess; see P2 note on CUID sources.) - Fix: ownership check `pids.includes(exam.patientId)` before rendering (same pattern as exam.routes.ts loadOwnedExam). ### P2 — HIGH (dynamically confirmed): `/api/patients/:id/photo` accepts ANY valid JWT for ANY patient — cross-tenant facial data (LGPD biometric) - `src/app.ts:296` + `src/middleware/auth.ts:24-34` (requirePhotoToken verifies signature+exp only; comment admits "Qualquer token válido (paciente OU médico) abre"). - PoC: attacker patient-JWT → victim photo 200 image/png; doctor-JWT → 200; no-token → 401. Also `/api/doctor/photo/:id` (doctor.routes.ts:455) same pattern for doctor photos. - Residual barrier = CUID guessability only. CUID v1 has timestamp+counter+hostname entropy; not safely enumerable blind. BUT victim patient CUIDs are legitimately exposed to: (a) any doctor the patient shared with (doctor.routes.ts:469 patient.id in list) — not attacker-reachable by choice; (b) P1 above returns patient-linked data by examId but does NOT echo patientId in output — checked; (c) `/api/items/explain` no; (d) shared-report HTML does not embed patient id. So practical exploitation needs a CUID from another bug (P1 gives exam→? no). Rate: High with the caveat; the middleware is a deliberate perf trade documented in code — reporting agent should rate accordingly and chain with any CUID-leak finding from BOLA agents. ### P3 — MEDIUM (dynamically confirmed): User enumeration on /api/auth/login + /api/auth/register + /api/auth/verify-email - `auth.routes.ts:100` (`user?.blocked` → 403 {blocked:true} BEFORE password check) — reveals account existence AND blocked status without credentials. - `auth.routes.ts:102` invalid_credentials (401) vs `auth.routes.ts:105` needsVerification (403, after correct password) — mixed but blocked/unverified branch is pre-auth. - `auth.routes.ts:243` register → 409 "Já existe conta com este e-mail" (confirmed 409 with valid body); `:244` 409 "CPF já cadastrado" (CPF oracle). - `auth.routes.ts:298` verify-email → 404 "Conta não encontrada" vs 401 wrong-code = clean existence oracle. - `doctor.routes.ts:309-311` doctor verify-email/google → 404/403 distinguish existing accounts (doctor google: "Nenhuma conta de médico com este e-mail"). - otp/request is generic (200 both) — good. otp/verify → 401 generic — good. forgot → generic — good. ### P4 — MEDIUM (dynamically confirmed): Stored HTML injection → XSS in shared report `/api/public/shared/:token` (doctor-facing) - `src/app.ts:455-460`: `patientName`, `exam.title`, `lab` interpolated UNESCAPED into HTML (only `a.contentMd` is escaped). Patient controls fullName (patient.routes.ts POST /) and exam title (extraction/user edit). - PoC: patient named `Attack` + exam title `Exame` → both raw in doctor's page (nameInjected=true, titleInjected=true). PIN-gate form action reflects `req.originalUrl` but URL-encoded — not exploitable via that path. - Impact: session/credential theft from the doctor viewing the shared link in a health context; page is served on the app origin. ### P5 — LOW/MEDIUM: `/api/doctor/invites/by-token/:token` returns patientName + doctor identity unauthenticated - `doctor.routes.ts:1243-1252`. Token entropy is good (2× randomUUID, `doctor.routes.ts:1225`) — not guessable; 404 vs 200 reveals only valid-token existence (by design for the landing). PII exposure limited to patient first/full name + doctor name/specialty/clinic to anyone holding the link (links travel via WhatsApp/email). LOW. ### P6 — LOW: `/api/health` + `/api/build-info` expose build/commit/branch + disk usage publicly - `app.ts` health route (~:150-180) returns version, commit, branch, builtAt, diskPct. Recon aid only; C:N per severity rubric. Informational. ### P7 — INFO (no PII): other public surfaces verified clean - decifre: no persistence, ipHash-only telemetry, 3/day/IP; response only echoes submitted values. lead: honeypot+idempotent 201, stores email+ipHash (marketing PII by consent; LGPD finalidade ok), same-response on duplicate (no enumeration). public-api v1: retail data only, x-api-key + balance gate (401 without key — confirmed); /exams/extract processes client-sent docs, response-only. labs: name/slug/aliases/logo only. doctor/crm: CFM public registry data only (name/specialty/situation). unsubscribe token: HMAC-SHA256(jwtSecret) + timing-safe compare — unforgeable; page shows only first name IF you already hold a valid token. swagger /api/docs: documents ONLY the public v1 API — no internal endpoints, examples are drug names/prices (no PII). errorHandler.ts: masks 500s in prod (message-only JSON), no stack in response. consulta.ts has NO raw res.json(e) leaks; other routes' next(e) funnel to errorHandler. - Shared-report token: `crypto.randomUUID() + '.' + expires` (analysis.routes.ts:278-282) = 122-bit random — unguessable; PIN `crypto.randomInt` 6-digit; PIN hash HMAC-SHA256(jwtSecret) keyed — offline brute-force impossible without secret (utils/crypto.ts:13-19); online PIN brute-force vs shareLimiter 10/15min ⇒ 1e6 PINs ≈ 2.9 years per link (IP-based limiter; proxy pools reduce but PIN+token both needed). Expiry enforced (410 confirmed). Cross-patient enumeration by token: impossible (findUnique on full random token). - OTP store: file-based, 6-digit CSPRNG, 10min expiry, 5-try lockout, 3/10min issue throttle — sound. MFA challenge: 32-byte token, 5 attempts, 5-min TTL — sound. ## Cross-check with BOLA agents P1 (consulta) is a BOLA-class bug surfaced by the PII lens — reporting agents for BOLA should own the report or dedupe against it; I did not file a report per my mandate. P2 chain-ready: if BOLA agents find any endpoint echoing foreign patient CUIDs (e.g. X-Patient-Id handling in exam list, measurement, mental-screening), chain with requirePhotoToken for facial-data CVSS. ## Dynamic-validation caveat All PoCs ran against the bundled app (esbuild, /tmp/srv) with test DB and test env (SMTP/S3 disabled). Behavior identical to prod paths for these routes (no mocks touched in them). vitest itself hangs in this sandbox (module resolution over the slow mount, ~39s per import); standalone node + bundle is the working harness pattern for other agents.
